summary: Implemented and verified Phase 9 of the 13-phase input-scoped gate invalidation plan (phases 1-8 landed in prior dispatches). A new interface-level regression suite (test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh, 17 cases, ~543s real wall time, 0 shellcheck findings) proves --skip-unchanged's real wiring across all 22 corpus-bearing gates: full real-interface treatment (mechanical corpus-violation re-run, six representative semantic seeded-violation cases spanning every corpus-declaration grammar shape, other-four-component sensitivity, negative case, mtime independence, determinism, and a realistic-sequence finding-set equivalence proof) for 18 of them, and composite-key-level-only treatment for the remaining 3 (gate 3: a genuine manifest-registration gap from this task's own earlier phases; gates 16/20: named pre-existing out-of-scope failures per the dispatch). This phase's own development surfaced and fixed two real, independently confirmed defects, each committed separately: a correctness bug in --skip-unchanged itself (combined with --only-gate/--max-cost, it was silently invalidating every unselected gate's valid cache entry, every run -- reproduced directly and fixed by gating the write/invalidate block on gate_selected()), and an unrelated pre-existing check-task-references.sh false positive in the exemption-taxonomy doc's own illustrative example. Four phases remain (10-13), covering JOBS_CAP re-derivation (which must now include this phase's own new suite in the pool aggregate), two evidence-gated derived phases, and the final redeploy/measurement that closes the task.
